name: The Golden Palace and the Ink Throat
title: Just Walk By My Side: A Gold Road, a King Made of Light, a Button, a Koopa Raid That Nobody Fully Planned, and the Grey Mario Who Ate the Sky
date: 20 Harvestide, 1040 BF — one day, from the morning road to the mid-afternoon sky (estimated; the account carries no clock, and was filed late, on 5 Aethel, after the studio account)
timeWindow: 20 Harvestide, 1040 BF, an archive estimate. The account carries no date or hour, and it reached the archive after the studio filing of 5 Aethel; the archive dates it earlier because the Mario it describes is not the one the studio produced, and the Koopa Troop's raid does not know a studio exists. 'The little ones are starting their morning play' puts the first meeting at about 09:30; the palace is 'almost visible in the midday sun'; the courtyard, stairs, hall and throne room take another hour; the raid and the service passage run to about 12:30; the flight and the cannon fill the afternoon. Anchored where it ends: about 14:30. Filed late and out of order; it does not move the world clock.
location: The Golden Palace, in the Golden Land (Mushroom Kingdom) — the road, the courtyard, the great hall, the throne room, the servants' passage, and the sky above
type: Infiltration / Koopa Raid / Collapse of a Location / Mario Arc
status: Filed — palace gone, King's light out, Bowser's ship in the air, and the only witness inside the mouth of the thing that did it
summary: A lost traveller named Jimmy Dobson meets a cheerful, grey Mario on a gold road, who walks him to a palace and a king made of light. Jimmy presses a button in his pocket; Bowser's Koopa Troop drops through the roof; a bomb goes off in the servants' passage; the host explains that he is a memory, grows an eye, and ends the King. Jimmy escapes on Bowser's airship, climbs into its cannon, and is fired into the creature's mouth.
description:
Waluigi opens this filing with the one sentence in the account that is also an instruction: **"Just walk by my side and everything will be alright."** A host said it on a gold road to a lost man, and by the end of the day the lost man was in a cannon, the host was a hand the size of the weather, and the road, the palace, the king and the sky had all been rubbed out in the order they were drawn.

This is not the studio. It is not the farm. It is a fourth place in the Mario file, in the Mushroom Kingdom, with a third Mario in it — grey from the cap down, introducing himself unasked and knowing every name — and a visitor who walked in on purpose with a button in his pocket. The party's other filings of the arc were found by accident. This one was walked into on a schedule.
outcome: The Golden Palace came down and the Golden Land's edges were seen peeling to white; the King's light went out; Bowser's raid failed or succeeded, depending on who was told what; and GB Mario, a third Mario beside the studio's two, ended the day claiming the sky. Jimmy Dobson was last seen inside him.
notableFeatures: A Mario who greets the visitor by name before the visitor gives it
A road of metal grass and chiming trees that ends in a palace
The King's throne room: 'IS THIS THE TRAVELER YOU PROMISED?'
A button in a pocket, and a raid that arrived on cue
Three plans in one hall: the King, the treasury, and the button
'Mario is... well, Mario is a memory.'
'Just the director making a final edit.'
'To stop a game, you gotta break the console.'
A cannon fired into the mouth of the thing that drew the world

participants.name: Jimmy Dobson
participants.role: Walked in as bait, squeezed the button, pressed it before the King, asked the question about the colours, hauled a trapped Koopa Troopa out of the stone, called for the anchor, and was fired from the ship's cannon into the creature's mouth.

participants.name: GB Mario
participants.role: Met the traveller on the road, walked him to the palace, protected him from the raid, admitted he was a memory, grew one eye, ended the Koopa car and the King's light, and reached for the ship out of the sky.

participants.name: The King of the Golden Land
participants.role: Sat the throne of light, asked for the promised traveller, fought off the Koopa raid and the creature at once, and went out.

participants.name: Bowser
participants.role: Dropped through the roof in a Koopa car, led Paratroopas, Hammer Bros and Troopers against the palace, lost the car, escaped by airship, and planned to turn the world to static to stop the creature.

reputationNotes._record: No standing moved: the Koopa Troop's casualties in the Golden Land are unfiled, the King had no faction, and the one witness who might say who commissioned the raid is inside a monster.

aftermath:
**The Golden Land is coming off the map.** The palace fell, the passages were seen peeling to white, and a grey stain spread from the site across the sky. Nothing in the account says where it stops.

**The Koopa raid came apart on its own orders.** The trooper did not know of an extraction, the pilot did not know of a bait, Bowser said he paid for a conquest and had missed pieces of the briefing. Three people on one ship were told three plans.

**A third Mario has been filed.** GB Mario is not the cape-wearing actor and not the studio's director. He calls himself a memory, explains the colours, and claims the final edit.

**Jimmy Dobson is inside him.** His badge, the button and whoever issued them are unfiled.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The plan had more authors than the day had hours.** The [[prop:prop_golden_raid_stated_objectives|reconciliation sheet]] is on file. The King expected a traveller, the host promised him, the troopers wanted a treasury, Bowser wanted the King, and the man with the button said it was planned. Nobody in the account saw the same plan twice. Waluigi trusts the button least, because it was the only part of the plan he can see.

**2. The colours are the clue.** The host was bright under the gold and grey in the passage. He said the colours belong to those inside the frame. The ship went grey from the nose back; the needles went to ink. The archive has seen two studios' worth of pixelated feathers. It had not seen the *world* lose its own pigment.

**3. 'Final edit' and 'master cut' arrive in the same afternoon.** One is the creature's own word, the other is the sky's. Waluigi has the Director on file with a remote and Evil Mario on file with a cape. This one has neither. He needs neither.

**4. 'I paid for a conquest.'** The most expensive sentence in the file. Whoever Bowser paid, they are not in the account.

**Recommendation:** find the badge. Find the briefing. Ask Bowser, separately, what he thought he bought. And do not fire anyone into a mouth again until somebody has read the label on the cannonball.
imageCaption: Just walk by my side. The road of pale gold, the metal trees ringing like bells, a grey Mario with his arms open, and a lost man stepping back with his fist closed in his pocket. The palace is already waiting at the end.
image_alt: Original scene illustration: a grey, colourless cartoon plumber spreads his arms in welcome on a golden road through a country of metal grass and bell-leaved trees, while a man in a dark jacket steps back with a hand in his pocket and a golden palace glows on the horizon.

sections.name: I. The Road That Was Already Waiting
sections.overview:
A road of pale gold ran across a country that was brighter than it had any right to be, and a man in a red cap was standing on it with his arms already open.

"Youve-a wondered far from home and got to-a land unlike-a your own," he said. "Have-a no fear because marios here and through my veneer your never a-lone."

[Jimmy Dobson](#/article/jimmy_dobson) said what a lost man says. "Oh thank god I've been lost here for ages."

[GB Mario](#/article/gb_mario) did not shake his hand. He leaned in, set one gloved hand on Jimmy's shoulder like a man steadying a ladder, and said it again in the gentler key: "its a me cant you see no tricks no plays no benevolence your free to stay." Jimmy asked him what free to stay meant, and the host laughed in a hum more than a sound. "Freedom is-a rare in this land. To find someone who wants to stay for nothing at all." The hand slid from shoulder to arm. It turned Jimmy toward the path. "Just walk by my side and everything will be alright."

Jimmy walked. Halfway down the first slope he looked back over his shoulder, and what he saw was road and dust and a light too flat to cast anything long. "Nothing to see back there but shadows and dust, dont you worry about it Jim," the host said, still facing forward, still smiling at the way ahead.

Jimmy had not said the word Jim. He had said Jimmy Dobson once, in a different tone, to nobody. He lifted his eyebrows and asked how the host knew. The laugh that answered was bright and enormous and entirely pleased with itself. "Whats the matter? Can't believe i knew it? Dont you worry about it being a little magic in-a the air! Dont think too hard about it, it'll only give you a headache!"

*WAH! 'Don't think too hard' is the first thing every landlord, magician and bad accountant says to a man who is thinking exactly hard enough. Jimmy was thinking exactly hard enough. I would like that on his headstone, with the dates left blank.*
sections.waluigi_note: A host who knows your name and tells you not to think about it has already done your thinking for you. The Golden Land is the first filed country that opened with a coat check.

sections.name: II. Wonders Around Every Corner
sections.overview:
The path wound deeper into gold, and the gold stopped looking soft. Up close the grass was thin shards of yellow metal, standing in blades. The trees carried metal leaves that rang like bells when they touched, and everything the sun fell on shone with an unnatural, blinding intensity.

"See!" said the host. "Nothing but wonders around every-a corner!" He gestured to a group of small colourful creatures fluttering between the trunks. "Look! The little ones are starting their morning play!"

Jimmy looked at the creatures. Then his right hand went into his pocket and closed around something there, and he held it.

The host walked on with a spring in his step, apparently blind to the shoulders that had gone stiff beside him. He stopped at a tree whose leaves chimed against each other like a tray of small bells. "They're quite-a charming little things aren't they? So much life and color in every corner of this kingdom!" A creature beside him chirped loudly and snapped its beak. "Go on, play! Play!"

"I dont think i want to play," Jimmy said, and squeezed the item in his pocket.

"Not playin' today, eh? No worries at all! There is-a plenty of ways to enjoy this beauty." The wink that went with it was meant to be teasing. "Perhaps we'll find you something a little more... exciting than playing games!" The chirping grew louder as he said it, a mix of high trills and clicking that bounced off the metal trunks and came back doubled.

Jimmy took one step back and let his shoulder slide out from under the hand. For a microsecond the grin failed. A look of gentle confusion crossed the host's face and was gone, replaced by the brightness. "Oh! Did I crowd you?" He took a small respectful step back himself and clasped his hands behind him, stiff as a doorman. "No harm done! I know its a lot to take in after being lost for-a so long. Take all the space you need."

*WAH! A creature snaps its beak, a man says 'go on, play', and the man squeezing the thing in his pocket says no. Whoever wrote this route had a very specific idea of who would turn up on it, and it was not Jimmy.*

sections.name: III. "Okay, Letsa Go"
sections.overview:
"But we shouldn't stand around forever," said the host. "Wouldn't you like to see the palace at least?"

"Palace?"

His excitement came back harder than before. "The golden palace! Can't you see it?" He pointed past the trees, where a distant silhouette sat on the horizon and glared with such strength it hurt to look at directly. "One of the greatest wonders of-a this world! It's where everything truly comes together!" He had to stop to catch his breath, and the cough that came out of him had a rhythm to it. "Once we arrive... well, let's just say the sights are well worth the walk!"

Jimmy took his hand out of his pocket. The item came with it. He looked at it a moment in the glare, and then he looked at the horizon, and then he said the words in the host's own accent, the way a man tries on a hat: "Okay letsa go."

The host beamed. His hand went out to pat Jimmy on the back and stopped an inch short, as though he had remembered something. "That's the spirit! Just like i knew you'd say!" He set off at a jaunty skip, and the stride quickened. "Don't worry, it's a lovely walk — short and sweet! We'll be there before you can say-a 'mamma mia'!"

It was not short. The trees gave way to gold mountains and the mountains closed into passes, and the ground in the passes was polished so flat that Jimmy could see his own face in every step he took. "Look! Can you feel it?" the host said, his voice vibrating with something close to mania. "The feeling that anything is possible?" He did not wait for an answer. A gate was rising ahead of them, golden, enormous, and the host stopped short in front of it with his body humming.

Jimmy looked down at what was in his hands.

"It's-a grand, isn't it? Just look at that craftsmanship!" The host turned and his eyes sparkled. "Did you see something interesting there? Don't hide it away! There are-a no secrets between friends here."

The gates answered before Jimmy did. Gold ground against gold with a deep, earth-shaking resonance, and the gate began to descend. "What's that noise?" Jimmy asked.

A quick reassuring pat on the back of Jimmy's hand. "Oh, that? It's just the gates finding their place! Nothing to be scared of, i promise! Big things often make a little noise when they arrive."

*WAH! 'There are no secrets between friends here.' He said it to a man with his fist closed on something. I have said it myself to men with their hands in their coats, and I never once said it to be answered.*

sections.name: IV. The Courtyard and the Stairs
sections.overview:
Jimmy went in first, cautiously, and the host came in at his heels — more shadow than companion. "Feel that? The air is different here, isn't it? More... alive." The gates ground shut behind them, and the sound of it echoed off the courtyard walls with a finality that settled in Jimmy's back teeth. "We've arrived at-a last! Stay close to me now. It's easy to get lost in such a big place."

In the full noon sun the host looked more vivid than anything around him. He stood very tall and very still, eyes on the palace stairs, and he looked almost as though he had been drawn into the world rather than born into it. When Jimmy looked at him closer, the stillness broke and the laugh came back — a hearty, over-bright sound that did not belong in a courtyard that solemn. "What is it? Is my mustache out of place? You're looking-a strange at me! Was it the excitement of the palace getting to you?"

"Sure," said Jimmy, and he followed.

The host took the marble stairs with confident purpose, the metal of his shoes clicking on gold-flecked stone, and his shadow lay long and sharp behind him in the noon. "Ready for a little royal hospitality? Every great visitor needs a place to rest, and the palace is filled with the finest things to offer!" He got to a pair of ornate doors and curled his fingers as if to knock. "Almost there! Just a few-a more steps!"

He did not knock. He beat Jimmy to the doors and shoved them open with a strength that made his cheer look like the smaller part of him. "Come on in! Make yourselves at home!" It was *yourselves*, plural, said to one man.

Inside, the hall ran so far away that the ground and the ceiling stopped being different things. The host stood in the middle of it counting the patterns in the gold overhead. "Is it everything you've ever dreamed of? It's really something special once you get used to the shine." He pointed down a long hall where torches burned with no fuel anybody could see. "There are dining halls, gardens... and the good room for sleeping! But the King likes to see guests first." His finger went up to a massive double stair that climbed higher. "Follow me!"

The silence in the hall was the silence of a place that swallows noise; it dampened even the breath of the man walking through it. The host climbed faster, and his shadow danced wildly over the golden walls with the torches. "Just wait until you meet-a him! He's always eager to meet anyone special who finds their way into the kingdom! He can be a little intense, but don't you worry about that! He means well."

At the head of the grand staircase a single set of doorbells began to ring on their own, one clear resonant note that went through the air and the floor. "Hear that? He's-a waiting for us!"

*WAH! Dining halls, gardens, and the good room for sleeping. Three promises, zero rooms. Waluigi has been in hotels with better follow-through and worse carpets.*
sections.waluigi_note: The host's sentences get faster as the building gets taller. He is not leading a tour. He is pushing a cart up a ramp.

sections.name: V. The King
sections.overview:
"The King?" Jimmy said.

The host smiled, and the smile reached his eyes and still did not soften the grin. "The King of this wonderful land! Wouldn't you want to meet the one who made all this possible?" His hand found the handle of the largest doors yet and paused there for just a moment, then went on. "Dont be nervous! Just be polite and let him do the talking. And oh!" The wink again. "Try not to lose your mind in all this gold!"

He threw the doors open and a blinding, heavy light came out into the hall.

The King was a mountain of a silhouette on a throne of pure light, so bright that his features would not stay still long enough to be read. The host went into a deep, sweeping bow. "Your Majesty, we have-a arrived!" He stepped aside to present his guest.

The King did not move. The temperature of the room went up as he settled his gaze on Jimmy. "MARIO..." The voice was heavy; it sounded in Jimmy's chest and not his ears. "IS THIS THE TRAVELER YOU PROMISED?"

Jimmy looked at the King for what he would later describe as exactly as long as it took. Then he pressed the button in his hand.

The host's face changed. The pleasant service came off it all at once, and his body snapped into a high alert, gloves straining. "Hey-a, what was that?" His hand went out toward Jimmy. "Don't do that! You don't know what you're doing!"

The King's light flared at the noise — not in anger, but in surprise. "WHAT IS THIS SOUND?" The ceiling of the hall rippled with it.

"Oh I know," Jimmy said, "and its planned. The koopa troops are coming."

*WAH! The ceiling rippled at a sound. I want that one entered carefully: a king whose roof moves when somebody presses a button is a king whose roof is not roof.*

sections.name: VI. The Raid
sections.overview:
Terror went over the host's face like a cloth. "Koopa troops? No, no, no, you can't do that! That's not-a how this works!" He lunged at Jimmy's hand to rip the button away, and his movements came out clumsy, as though he were fighting through thick molasses.

"WHO SPEAKS OF SUCH WAR IN MY PRESENCE?" The King's voice dropped to a terrifying rumble and the light of the throne began to pulse in a violent, jagged rhythm. "MARIO! EXPLAIN THIS TREASON!"

The castle trembled with a distant booming. It was not Jimmy's pulse; it was something much bigger and harder, and it was walking. "They're gonna tear it all down!" the host shouted, voice cracking. "Everything you-a see!"

Jimmy started to say something about what had happened to Peach — *after Peach's deat-* — and the roof burst open before the sentence did.

Engines roared through the hole. Debris came down on the marble in a shower, and a Koopa car dropped out of the sky and skidded to a halt between the host and the throne with its headlights dazzling like bullets. "BOWSER!" the host yelled, ducking behind his own palms.

"HAHA! NICE PLACE YOU GOT HERE, MARIO!" [Bowser](#/article/bowser) rumbled, hands on the car's sides, face tipped up toward the light. "TOO BAD IT'S ABOUT TO BURN!"

"YOU!" The King's light flared white and unstable. "YOU BRING THIS STAIN INTO MY HOUSE?"

The host grabbed Jimmy's arm and pulled him back from the machine. "We have to-a get out! The whole place is-a falling apart!"

"Hey!" Jimmy said. "Wait, help!"

"I'm-a trying! Just stay-a close to me!" The grip tightened painfully. He ignored the cry. Bowser stamped the accelerator and the sound rolled like thunder in the dying hall. "MOVE IT, MARIO! GET OUT OF THE WAY OR GET CRUSHED!"

The King answered in a voice that shook the air. "THESE ARE NOT INVITED GUESTS! BEGONE FROM MY SIGHT!" A wave of shimmering, solid light burst off the throne and hit the front of the car.

Then the rest of the raid arrived. Paratroopas dropped from the broken roof in a swarm of parachutes; Hammer Bros lined the ceiling ridges and began lofting heavy hammers into the hall with a methodical "TARGETS SPOTTED!"; Bowser dodged a volley of his own side's hammers and swore at them. The host dragged Jimmy behind a falling marble pillar. "THEY'RE HIT-TING EVERYWHERE!" The front doors burst. Koopa Troopas poured through the gate in boots, shouting that it was time to raid the treasury, and Bowser barked over them: "NOT THE TREASURY! GO FOR THE KING!"

The King took them all at once. His light pulsed, a wave of heat knocked a rank of intruders backward, and the golden radiance extended out toward Bowser's men in sweeping bars. "DO YOU THINK YOUR CHAOS CAN SHATTER ME?"

*WAH! Look at the order. Roof, car, hammers, front gate, treasury. Everyone at that raid had a different idea of what it was for. Bowser wanted the King, the troopers wanted the gold, and the man who set it off wanted a button pressed. That is not one plan. That is three plans sharing a ladder.*
sections.waluigi_note: A raid with one target and three motives will always feel like a mob. The tell is the treasury shout: somebody on the Koopa side was told the wrong objective, or was told none.

sections.name: VII. The Service Door
sections.overview:
The host stayed low to the floor, shielding Jimmy with his body. "EVERYWHERE! IT'S EVERY-AWHERE!" His eyes were bright with a frantic alarm that looked, for the first time, entirely real. "WE GOTTA MOVE NOW!" The marble cracked and buckled under them. The hall was a cacophony of hammer strikes, car horns and royal light, and the host dodged a tumbling Koopa Troopa and pointed at a small service door behind a fallen pillar. "WE GO THERE!"

He dragged Jimmy along with his boots digging at the fracturing floor, shoved aside a piece of fallen marble, and reached for the handle. A hammer came out of nowhere and bit into the floor between them and the exit. "GET BACK!" He cursed and put his shoulder into the door.

Jimmy said, to nobody, "The ambush. It... its working. I think."

The host's head snapped round. His eyes narrowed. "Ambush? What-a are you talking about?"

He did not get an answer; a volley of hammers whistled overhead and Bowser's voice came through the wall: "THIS IS NO FUN! WHERE ARE THE REINFORCEMENTS?!" and then the sound of the Koopa car meeting a marble pillar. The King's reply was a scream: "YOU'VE-A BROUGHT CHAOS UPON MYSELF! I WILL HAVE YOUR HEADS!" His light became an uncontrolled blaze that began to sear the stone.

Another explosion rang out from the hallway behind the front entrance, much closer than the last. The host looked at Jimmy. "WAIT! DID YOU-A DO THIS?"

"Uhh no," said Jimmy.

The host stared for a suspicious heartbeat. Another tremor settled the argument. "NO TIME FOR LIES!" He pulled Jimmy through the service door and the latch clicked shut behind them in a much tighter, dimmer servants' passage. The sound of Bowser's engine shook the wall beside their heads. Then something thumped against the door from the outside, several rapid blows, and the host's voice rose in real surprise. "OPEN THE DOOR! IT'S-A US!" He stopped. "WHO-A ELSE IS COMING?!"

The door flew inward, shredded by a bomb.

Splinters filled the passage. A group of Koopa Troopa squad leaders rolled in through the smoke with scratched shells and popped up out of their rolls. "Room's a mess!" one of them snarled, and another pointed a staff at the host. "Back off, mustache! We're on official business!"

"OFFICIAL?!" The host put his hands up. "SINCE WHEN DOES BOWSER-A LEAD THE TROOPS WITH EXPLOSIVES?!"

*WAH! 'Who else is coming?' He asked it in the voice of a man at his own door. This is the first line in the entire account where the host does not know the next one.*

sections.name: VIII. Black and White
sections.overview:
From the main hall came a deafening crack as the King's form slipped its grip, his golden light snapping like breaking glass. "IT IS NOT DONE!" The voice was desperate now. "YOU SHALL ALL BURN!" The squad leaders traded a look. If the King was losing it, one of them said, they had better get out; before he could turn, a barrage of flying magic lights began hitting the corridor around them.

Jimmy looked at the man who had walked him in. The passage had no gold in it, and without the gold there was no colour in him either. He was grey. He was grey from cap to boots, and the colour had been going in [[prop:prop_golden_land_colour_continuity|a straight line since the courtyard]]; the red was not in the cap and the blue was not in the overalls. Jimmy said what he had not asked in two hours of walking.

"Mario, I've never asked this, but why are you black and white?"

The host froze. He stared at Jimmy with a look of sudden, heavy realisation. "It's-a because this place isn't real, Jimmy Dobson! It's not real!" He laughed in a breathy, strained way. "The colors... they only happen for those who belong in-a the frame. But once the curtain pulls back... the truth comes out."

"WHAT ARE YOU BABBLING ABOUT?" Bowser rumbled from down the hall through the smoke. "GET THE REINFORCEMENTS NOW!"

The host stepped closer, black-and-white eyes wide and sincere. "Don't-a look too closely at the colors anymore. Once you see they're fake, it's hard to look at anything else."

"Your not really Mario are you," Jimmy said.

The host pulled back. A long, pained shadow stretched against the monochrome wall. "The question is... are you really anything at all if you're just looking for a villain to hate?" The smile had turned thin and bitter and the charm was gone from it. "Mario is... well, Mario is a memory."

"MARIO! STOP CHATTING AND MOVE!" Bowser's engine revved down the corridor. From the great hall the King's voice came back, almost mechanical now. "GET THEM! DISMANTLE THE TREASON!" A blast of light shattered a section of the ceiling and showered masonry on the Koopa squads.

"Move, fast!" He grabbed Jimmy's wrist again and pulled him into the dark of the tunnel.

Jimmy spoke to the back of his head as they ran. "You know our intel suggested it was just you here. No king, no castle. But it seems like we were wrong."

The host did not break stride, but his voice dropped to a gritty, dispassionate whisper. "Intel is just another name for fiction when you're staring at a god's light. Told you no matter what happened, you'd never be alone." He jerked Jimmy behind a heavy golden crate. "Shh! Stay low!"

*WAH! 'Our intel suggested it was just you here.' Jimmy had a map that said one man, no castle. He had a button, a badge, and a briefing. He did not have a palace. Whoever wrote the briefing was not looking at the same country. I have read some of my own reports like that and I would like it noted that I fired myself for it.*
sections.waluigi_note: Two answers in a row, and both of them were honest: the place is not real, and I am a memory. The first lie of the whole day was the one he told for two hours, and it was the first one that Jimmy checked.

sections.name: IX. "Do You Like Games?"
sections.overview:
"I look to Mario," Jimmy would say, afterwards, "and I ask: you can take on the Koopa, right?"

The grin that answered was more grin than joy. The host leaned back against the crate and chuckled low. "Can I take 'em on?" he said. "In this world, I can do whatever they wrote in the handbook for me."

The sound of the main hall sharpened. Bowser's machine strained somewhere at an incline: "GET IN THE WAY!" and the scream of grinding metal. A rush of golden light swept the tunnel, thick and blinding, and the King's voice came from under their feet. "THROUGH THE EARTH, THEY SHALL BE CRUSHED!" The ground shuddered under the magic.

The host turned around, and his form distorted.

"Oh what's that matter," he said, "you don't want to-a play, Bowser?" His face lengthened. His bones creaked like old floorboards. He grew to monstrous proportions, the darkness in the tunnel closing about him, and the smile on that dark face was huge, and the only other feature on it was a single eye. "Well than... lets-a play."

"WHAT THE-A...?" Bowser's engine sputtered and died. He stared up at the towering, one-eyed mass that had been the man beside Jimmy. "MARIO?! WHAT ARE YOU?"

"TRAITOR!" The King's voice screamed from the hall, and the golden light went to violent rays that lashed the walls. "YOU ARE NOT EVEN OF THE SAME WORLD!"

The monster took a heavy step toward Bowser, the ground cracking under its weight. "So... tell me, little turtle-man... do you like games??"

Bowser's hand trembled visibly on the gear shift. "HEY! BACK OFF! WHAT KIND OF MAGIC TRICK IS THIS?!" The King lashed at the new shadow with desperate radiance. "YOUR MAGIC IS A BLIGHT! YOU ARE AN ERROR IN THE FABRIC OF THIS WORLD!"

The single eye narrowed on the light. "An error?" The voice rattled Jimmy's teeth. "No... just the director making a final edit."

It lunged at the Koopa car with terrifying speed and the car went onto its side. Bowser swung a hammer at a mass that was not flesh, more like trying to hit a shadow. "Let's-a play for real now!" The roar was jarring and unearthly. The King impaled it with beams of solid radiance, and the thing laughed as the light went through. "Does that hurt? Or is it just another special effect?"

Jimmy, behind the crate, said: "So this is what he meant by no benevolence."

The eye rolled back toward him for a flicker of recognition. "Did you want a hero, Jim?" The voice was a blend of charming plumber and something primal and hateful. "Heroes always have-a something to hide. Don't you?"

Bowser scrambled out of the wreckage with his eyes darting. "SHOW YOURSELF!" The golden throne began to spill liquid fire across the floor. "MY WORLD SHALL NOT END IN A SHADOW!" The monster focused on the King. "Then end the show!" it said, and lunged into the spreading light, screaming.

*WAH! Director. Final edit. Special effect. He used the word 'effect' about a god's light. The last Mario in my files who talked like that was holding a remote, and he walked out of a studio with it in his hand. This one is not holding anything. That is worse.*
sections.waluigi_note: The archive now has three Marios who sound like crew. Evil Mario takes direction. Director Mario gives it. This one edits. If somebody is cutting the footage, it is the third one, and he is calling it a play.

sections.name: X. The Run
sections.overview:
Jimmy ran, and kept running.

The service passages carried the noise of it behind him in pieces: crashing thunder, roaring vehicles, divine screaming. "IT'S OVER!" The King's voice seemed to fold in on itself, followed by a blinding flash of white that went through the stone. "YOU HAVE BROUGHT NOTHING BUT VOID!" Behind him, from the throne room, rose the creature's mocking laugh, climbing in pitch. "Hahaha! Don't worry! It won't stay empty for long!"

The corridor began to shake with a tectonic force. Dust fell in sheets. Somewhere in the smoke one of Bowser's troops was crying, "Where did they go?! The machine's blown! We're stuck!" Jimmy grabbed the nearest voice and hauled.

"HEY! LET GO!" The Koopa Troopa scrambled to pull his shell out of the grip. "I'm too busy being pinned by all this rubble! Get your hands off me, civilian!"

The corridor behind them erupted in a shockwave that dropped the ceiling closer. The King's screaming stopped; where it had been there was a profound silence from the palace's centre. "Something's wrong," the soldier muttered, staring at the dark ahead. "The light... it went out. Why did the light go out?!"

Jimmy took out [[prop:prop_jimmy_dobson_badge|his badge]]. "I am on your side, dumbass."

"A badge?" The soldier stared at the insignia. "You're part of the command? I didn't know about an extraction mission!" His leg was caught under a block of fallen ceiling, and he began to struggle up with real hope. A rumble went through the building that was not building — a sound like heavy paper being torn. "GUARDS!" Bowser's voice came down the passage. "RETREAT TO THE TRUCKS! SHE'S GOING DOWN!"

"Bowser," Jimmy shouted toward it. "The ambush we planned to take Mario's castle. We're retreating???"

The soldier's hands clutched his arm. "Bowser? I don't know who YOU think you're talking to, but this isn't a planned retreat! The castle is literally being swallowed by shadow!" From the hall ahead Bowser's voice raged back: "I'M NOT RETREATING FROM A TINY WHITE HAT! I'M GETTING OUT BEFORE THIS WHOLE DAMN PLACE DISAPPEARS!"

A fissure ripped across the floor and nearly took the soldier whole. Jimmy hauled him out of the stones, shell scraped. "Watch the shell! Damn it, watch the shell!" They ran. The walls changed as they ran: the rock did not crack now, it peeled away in flat, untextured sheets. "Wait," the soldier whimpered, glancing at the void behind a layer of stone that had come off like paper. "What's happening to the walls? Why is there nothing behind them?!"

"It's a trap," said Jimmy.

*WAH! A trap. He said it as a guess and it was the best one on the road. I would like the record to show that the man with the badge and the plan was the last to learn the place was a drawing.*

sections.name: XI. The Ship and the Grey Stain
sections.overview:
The smoke parted for half a second and showed the colossal metal nose of Bowser's fighter ship pressing against the tunnel ceiling. "HOLD ON!" Bowser's voice boomed from the cockpit. "GET IN OR STAY IN THE HOLE!" From the collapsing centre of the palace came the other voice, the one that had been Mario's, ripping through the air with more mania than before. "Don't leave yet, friends! The best part is-a just starting!"

Jimmy ran for the ship and shouted at it. "Deploy the anchor!"

"Anchors? What are you blathering about?!" Bowser roared, and he slammed a lever down in the same breath. The ship tilted. A heavy-duty metal claw thundered down from the undercarriage and struck the stone with an ear-splitting boom. "GRAB ON!" the soldier screamed, and threw himself at the ramp as the tunnel began to dissolve into nothing. In the shifting geometry of the dying palace a massive, single-eyed shadow swung through the debris toward the ship. "Don't-a go so soon!" Its voice peeled like old film.

Jimmy grabbed on. The soldier hauled himself up the ramp and kicked out to yank Jimmy inside as the ceiling came down. "WE'RE LOSING THE CLAW!" Bowser shouted at the controls. The ship lurched upward on its engines with the anchor dragging, and through the glass of the cockpit the shadow clung to the very edge of the structure with its eye fixed on the ship's tail. Behind the anchor, where the ground had been, there was only a bottomless white void.

The ship broke into clear sky. "What the hell happened?" Jimmy said. "I did everything you said."

The soldier stared at him, shell-shocked. "Everything I said? I never said a damn word to you!"

"The raid on the castle. I was meant to be the bait, no? He led us straight to the king and played us like a fiddle."

"Bait?" Bowser slammed another lever. "If that's true, then we were all fools! I didn't pay for a trap, I paid for a conquest!" The soldier laughed in a hysterical, jagged way. "Look at the sky! The world didn't even hide, it just gave up!" The pilot's eye rolled to the horizon. "He's right, sir. That wasn't just an attack. That was an ending."

"SILENCE!" Bowser said. Jimmy stayed quiet, as instructed. *This was Bowser's plan, wasn't it?* "Just thinking," Bowser muttered, to himself more than anyone. "I missed a few pieces from the briefing. Had to pivot on the fly."

High above, a strange grey streak of nothingness began to bleed into the clear sky from the direction the palace used to stand. "Bowser," the pilot said, pointing. "Is that the weather?"

"Weather?!" Bowser snatched the pilot's hand and threw it down. "The sky is bleeding shadow and you're calling it weather?!" The streak broadened like a stain spreading through water. "It's the nothingness!" the soldier howled. "It's taking everything!" A much larger rift cut across the grey, and through it, for a heartbeat, a pale translucent eye peered, just as huge as the monster in the palace. "HE'S-A COMING!" The voice came from the sky itself.

"Wait," Jimmy said. "That accent. It's Mario, isn't it? I'm not sure how we stop him."

*WAH! Bowser said 'I paid for a conquest'. Paid whom? There is a receipt in that sentence and nobody is holding it. Also he said 'a few pieces from the briefing'. Same briefing? Different briefing? Waluigi needs a room with a long table.*
sections.waluigi_note: Three men on one ship, each told the plan by someone else, each sure someone else wrote it. The soldier never heard of an extraction. The pilot never heard of a bait. The king never heard of a conquest. Jimmy was the only person aboard who thought the plan was his own.

sections.name: XII. The Master Cut
sections.overview:
Bowser's head snapped round with a look of pure loathing. "Stupid questions when things are falling apart!" He ground his teeth, every inch a man who has lost his grip on a game. "To stop a game, you gotta break the console! Keep your head down and shut up!"

"Breaking the console?" The soldier's voice rose as the ship lurched. "What the hell does that even mean?!" The sky above began to ripple and the colours to wash out into a jagged monochrome mess. "HE'S-A PLAYING!" the giant voice boomed in the rift. "IT'S THE MASTER-A CUT!"

"You're not thinking of doing that, are you?" Jimmy asked.

Bowser made a sound that was half snort and half growl, his fingers tight on the joystick. "Think I'm playing games with you?" He glanced back with a terrifying, manic grin. "Everything's been a game! Everything's been a stupid little setup! If I have to turn the whole world to static to win, then I'll do it!"

"STOP IT!" The soldier pointed at the windscreen as the frame of the ship began to pixelate and glitch. The nose flattened like ink under a brush, steel grey to a flat black-and-white sketch. "WE'RE LOSING DETAIL!" the pilot cried. The needles on the gauges had thinned into hand-drawn lines of ink. The plane's wing jittered until Jimmy felt it in his own chest. "We either burn the world down," Bowser said, his voice going scratchy like vinyl, "or let it blink us out of existence!"

A massive charcoal-coloured hand began to descend through the clouds. "HE IS-A REACHING!" the voice of the monster thundered. "WAIT-A MINUTE, DON'T END THE STORY YET!"

"There it is," said Jimmy.

The hand came down with a roar like rushing wind. Close up it was a sketch — heavy, jagged brushstrokes that shadowed out the sky. "HOLD THE LINE!" Bowser bellowed, hauling the controls left. "DO NOT LET IT GRAB US!" The pilot screamed that the controls were static; there was no resistance, nothing felt real. The soldier curled into a shivering knot with his mouth open in a silent scream. The hand stopped inches from the cockpit glass, motionless and menacing, and the voice said: "READY OR NOT... HERE I COME!"

Jimmy took hold of the ship's cannon. It was freezing, a flat textured block of black ink. "WHY ARE YOU GRABBING THAT? IT DOESN'T EVEN WORK!" Bowser yelled. "It's part of the world," the soldier whimpered. "If it's here, it's real... right?" The fingers brushed the cockpit windows with a hollow sound, like paper on wood. "GET THE GUNS READY!" Bowser's voice cracked. "IF THE PRINCIPAL WANTS TO PLAY, WE'LL-A GIVE HIM A SURPRISE!"

Jimmy took the cannonball out. He called a soldier over and told him to fire it up at the monster; he would put an end to this himself. The soldier looked at him wide-eyed. "You mean... the heavy ordnance? But the firing mechanism is-a glitching!" "DON'T JUST STAND THERE!" Bowser roared. Jimmy's hands were on the ammunition, and it was heavy, cold, and felt like a dense, physical knot of ink. The face appeared in the clouds, massive, grinning with its single eye. "HERE I COME! THE FINALE!"

"I climb into the cannon with the cannonball," said Jimmy.

"WHAT ARE YOU DOING?!" The soldier recoiled in horror as Jimmy squeezed into the chamber. "YOU'LL GET KILLED!" "DO IT!" Bowser bellowed over the lurch of the ship tipping into the giant hand. "WE'VE GOT NOTHING LEFT BUT THAT!" "GOING, GOING, GONE!" the creature laughed. The soldier's trembling fingers found the firing lever. "HOLD ON TO SOMETHING! I'M-A FIRING!"

There was no sound of a launch. There was a bone-shattering blast of kinetic force like gravity closing its fist, and the soldier was thrown back against the bulkhead shouting *NOOOOO*. Jimmy went into the dark — not through a tunnel but through the idea of space — at a speed that smeared the monochrome world into a single grey streak. "YOU THINK YOU'RE-A THE PLAYER?!" The monster's voice shook his skull. "COME AND GET ME!"

"Oof," said Jimmy, flying through the sky. "This was a bad idea."

The eye filled his sight. Up close it was not an eye. It was a swirling vortex of white and black, an iris made of thousands of tiny dancing figures. The face split in a grin of granite teeth. "BRING IT! SHOW ME THE-A ACTION!"

"Okay," said Jimmy. "This is a bad idea. Put me back out. Put me back out. Aaaa—"

"TOO LATE!" The grin widened until the mouth began to swallow the sky. "THE PROTAGONIST ALWAYS LOSES IN THE END!" Jimmy's momentum stalled against a barrier of thick, tar-like substance; he was not flying now, he was sinking, into the dark of a throat. "OOOH... THAT TICKLES!" The laugh went through him like a strike on a gong. "YOU'RE-A TINY! SO TINY!"

As he struggled he could see the tongue. It was not flesh. It was thick, heavy sweeps of charcoal and ink.

*WAH! The protagonist always loses in the end. He said it to a man in a cannon. It is the only sentence in the account that was delivered in the right tense: a promise from the thing doing the drawing. And the man who was supposed to be bait is now the lodger.*
sections.waluigi_note: Fired into a mouth with his own ammunition. Waluigi would like it recorded that it is the same cannon, the same ink and the same man, in that order, and that the one who set the order was the Mario who is a memory.

gallery.alt: A battered Koopa airship lies nose-down over a white void while a huge ink-and-charcoal hand and a single-eyed grinning face fill the sky, and a tiny figure leaps from the cannon's mouth.
gallery.caption: The finale as the account paints it: the ship losing its detail, the hand stopping inches from the glass, one eye, and the speck in front of the cannon. The palace glows on the horizon as it was last seen.

gallery.alt: A grey cartoon plumber with a push broom bows and sweeps an arm toward a throne of white-gold light while a man in a dark jacket leans in the doorway with a thumb on a small button.
gallery.caption: The question and the button. 'Your Majesty, we have-a arrived' on one side of the room, and on the other a man who has already decided.

gallery.alt: A spiked Koopa kart-car crashes through a golden hall roof as Paratroopas drop, Hammer Bros throw from the rafters and two figures run behind a marble pillar.
gallery.caption: The roof, on cue. Bowser through the gold, the swarm behind him, and the three plans in the hall that did not agree.

gallery.alt: A man in a dark jacket hauls a Koopa Troopa along a servants' passage whose stone walls peel away in sheets to blank white, with a huge eye looming in smoke behind them.
gallery.caption: The honest part of the building. Plain stone peeling off a void, a badge that worked on the wrong trooper, and the eye in the smoke.

gallery.alt: A towering grey one-eyed monster stoops over an overturned Koopa kart-car in a ruined golden tunnel while a hammer passes through its body and beams of light pass straight through.
gallery.caption: 'Well than lets-a play.' The Mario who was a memory, the car on its side, and a hammer going through a shadow.

gallery.alt: A tiny man in a dark jacket sinks into black tar inside a gigantic charcoal-and-ink throat, with a white circle of sky far ahead.
gallery.caption: 'You're-a tiny! So tiny!' The tongue is charcoal, the walls are ink, and the way out is a circle of sky getting smaller.

xpAwards.name: Jimmy Dobson
xpAwards.title: Event - The Golden Palace and the Ink Throat - the Button
xpAwards.desc: Walked into the Golden Land as bait with a detonator in his pocket, kept his nerve for two hours of the host's patter, and pressed it in front of the King: the roof came down on cue.

xpAwards.name: Jimmy Dobson
xpAwards.title: Event - The Golden Palace and the Ink Throat - the Run
xpAwards.desc: Dragged a pinned Koopa Troopa out of a collapsing servants' passage by showing a badge and swearing at him, called the anchor, and climbed into a cannon to meet the thing that ate the sky.

name: The Locked Cottage, the Hypno-Helmet, and the Dragon at the Goblin Camp
title: The Locked Cottage, the Hypno-Helmet, and the Dragon at the Goblin Camp: A Bonding Ritual, a Borrowed Bean Disguise, and the Hour-Long Map
date: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — estimated next-day continuation from Bones's tree-rest on 1 Aethel; the final map beat may cross midnight, but no hour or boundary is recorded
timeWindow: Begins at an unknown hour on 2 Aethel and continues through the night to the goblin camp; the map is measured for one hour. No exact clock reading or midnight crossing is supplied.
type: Session Event / Escape, Ritual, and Unresolved Dragon Summons
location: Unnamed Material-plane cottage, Fawful-aligned compound, woodland, and goblin camp; no route between them or canonical site name is established
status: Bones escapes and ends in the trees still disguised; Fawful's ritual remains unresolved, and a dragon leaves with an Archie-like camp figure whose identity is not confirmed
summary: After the previous Bones filing leaves him sleeping in trees beyond the Legion wall, this account opens in a locked cottage far from it, with two armed Toad guards calling his confinement a ‘bonding ritual.’ A failed key swipe gives way to an emergency-release button that unlocks every door. Outside, a green-cloaked figure and a figure called Mimbus appear near Fawful’s declaration, ‘I HAVE DRAGONS.’ A Fawful hypno-helmet drone attacks an unidentified person; its vines lash Bones before an older woman and a fox-eared Toad help remove the helmet. The conversation invokes the Emerald Enclave, a closed door to new members, and a plan to stop Fawful’s forces from completing a dragon-linked ritual. The possible dragon connection to Bowser’s Castle before 1035 is not proven. Bones accepts a recorded 20-gold payment, takes a Bean guard’s outer disguise but leaves the shorts, escapes through a broken window, and later slips away from Fawful’s sacrifice preparations and a mustard-spraying clockwork drone. A camp-side fart-spray gag is also recorded, though its user and target are unclear. At an unnamed goblin camp, an Archie-like bot douses the fire with ‘WATERBALL!’ and wins a place among the goblins. A dragon then arrives asking for Archie and leaves with an Archie-like figure after an offer of training; neither figure is reconciled with Archie Miser. Bones declines, sleeps in the trees still disguised, and spends one hour measuring a map whose route and scale are not recorded.
description: The previous Bones filing closes with him under the trees, beyond the Legion wall but not beyond anyone else's reach. This account begins after a gap the notes do not bridge: Bones wakes in a cottage with two armed Toad guards and locked doors. The route from the tree to the room is not supplied, and the archive will not invent one. What follows is a chain of escapes under Fawful's pursuit, an offered ‘bonding ritual,’ a threatened sacrifice, and a dragon who comes looking for an Archie. The record keeps the green-cloaked figure, the older woman, the guards, the drone's victim, and the camp's Archie-like figure at the level of identification the notes support. It also keeps the dragon separate from the Bowser's Castle record until someone can prove the match.
outcome: Bones escapes the cottage and Fawful's ritual site, survives the drone pursuit, and reaches a goblin camp. The camp's Archie-like figure leaves with a dragon; the dragon's identity, the passenger's identity, and the ritual's outcome remain unresolved. Bones ends in the trees wearing the borrowed Bean disguise, with a map he measured for one hour.
imageCaption: Two armed Toad guards hold Bones inside the locked cottage; the emergency-release button is within reach, but the exit remains shut.
image_alt: Bones stands between two armored Toad guards in a locked cottage with a small release button beside the door.

gallery.alt: Bones faces a crawling hypno-helmet drone as mechanical vines reach across the room; a fox-eared Toad watches from the doorway
gallery.caption: Beat IV — the helmet is torn free, but the device has already turned its vines toward Bones.

gallery.alt: Bones in borrowed Bean guard clothes climbs through a broken window while a fox-eared Toad and an older woman are escorted away
gallery.caption: Beat VI — Bones keeps the guard's outer clothes, leaves the shorts, and uses the broken window.

gallery.alt: Disguised Bones turns from a hulking Bean guard as a clockwork drone vents a yellow cloud and Fawful directs the pursuit
gallery.caption: Beat VII — the mustard drone buys Fawful's forces time; Bones is looking for a gap, not a victory.

gallery.alt: A grey-green dragon and an Archie-like rider arrive at a forest goblin camp beside a steaming, doused fire while Bones watches
gallery.caption: Beat IX — a dragon leaves with someone the camp calls Archie; the image reference is a possible likeness, not an identity finding.

notableFeatures: The opening is after the prior tree-rest, but the record gives no route or elapsed interval from the Legion wall to the cottage.
A failed key swipe is followed by a successful emergency-release button that unlocks every door.
The hypno-helmet drone is filed separately from the 1035 Fawthful Castle drone; the source does not establish that they are the same machine.
The fox-eared Toad may resemble roster #73, Toad ie Foxx, but ‘Konathin’ and the unclear ‘Toad ie Fox’ wording are not reconciled; the roster remains unseen.
The dragon is said to resemble the one used at Bowser's Castle before 1035, but no identity match is established; the Archie-like bot and passenger are likewise not reconciled with Archie Miser.
The account records a 20-gold payment and an unquantified camp-side gold transaction; it does not establish an audited end balance.
A fart-spray gag occurs in the camp-side sequence; the source does not establish its user, target, or effect, so it is not assigned to a character or added as inventory.

sections.name: I. A Cottage Far from the Legion Wall
sections.imageCaption: The distance from the wall is certain; the route from Bones's tree-rest to this cottage is not recorded.
sections.overview:
The previous Bones filing left him asleep in the trees after turning away from the Legion wall. This one opens somewhere else: Bones wakes in a cottage, far from the wall he had just left. The record never explains the transfer. There is no marked road, no named guide, no time spent traveling. The gap stays a gap.

Two armed Toad guards hold the room. Both doors are locked. When Bones asks what is happening, the explanation he receives is a **‘bonding ritual.’** The phrase is preserved because it is the explanation the guards gave, not because it explains the locks, the distance, or the weapons. Their names and their reason for holding him are not recorded. Neither guard is promoted to a known character by standing near a door.
sections.waluigi_note: A locked cottage and two armed guards are confinement. Calling it a ‘bonding ritual’ does not make the hinges less honest.

sections.name: II. The Failed Swipe and the Button That Opened Every Door
sections.overview:
Bones tried the key swipe. It failed; the door stayed locked. The account does not say whether the swipe was a card, a borrowed credential, or some other access gesture, so the archive records the failed attempt and leaves the object unnamed.

Then Bones found the emergency-release button. The cottage's own explanation was unusually clear on that point: it released all the doors from being locked. He pressed it. The locks opened. Not just the one in front of him—all the doors.

The button was not a key, and it did not tell him who had brought him there. It did give him a way out. Bones took it, and the story moved from a room with two armed guards to the ground outside without furnishing a map of the route between them.
sections.waluigi_note: The swipe did nothing. The button did everything. Waluigi would like the builders of the cottage to explain why the emergency release was easier to reach than the exit.

sections.name: III. The Green Cloak, Mimbus, and Fawful's Claim
sections.overview:
At the tree line, Bones saw an unnamed figure in a green cloak. Mimbus was named near that sighting, but the account does not describe the cloaked figure's face, allegiance, or relation to the other person. It also does not say whether this Mimbus is the historical operative from the 1035 false-heir scheme or another figure using the same name.

Fawful's words arrive as a claim: **‘I HAVE DRAGONS.’** The shout marks the threat that hangs over the next scenes. It does not, on its own, prove the ritual has worked, that the speaker has a dragon under control, or that the cloaked figure is part of his force. Bones does not stop to solve the cast list while the compound is active around him.
sections.waluigi_note: A boast is evidence that someone made a boast. It is not a custody chain for a dragon.

sections.name: IV. The Hypno-Helmet Drone
sections.imageCaption: Bones moves toward the helmeted victim as the fox-eared companion and an older woman reach the room; neither companion's identity is settled.
sections.overview:
A **Fawful hypno-helmet drone tackled an unnamed person.** The machine forced its helmet down over the victim's head. The notes describe the drone as eating the person's brain; no name, anatomy, or medical outcome follows that line, and the archive adds none.

Bones ran in. The device sent vines out and slashed at him: **the drone's vines lashed at Bones.** The older woman and the fox-eared Toad also moved into the room. Between them, the helmet was pulled off the victim. The drone scurried away before Bones could establish what happened to the person underneath it.

This machine is not filed as the Fawthful drone first seen in Bowser's Castle in 1035. That older record describes a small surveillance drone; it says nothing about hypnosis, helmets, brain-feeding, or vines. The new device gets its own entry, and its current location remains unknown.
sections.waluigi_note: A helmet removed is not the same thing as a victim recovered. The drone escaped, the person is unidentified, and nobody filed a medical report.

sections.name: V. The Emerald Enclave and the Dragon-Summoning Stakes
sections.overview:
The woman and the fox-eared companion spoke of the **Emerald Enclave**. Their account says the group had stopped letting new people in. The notes do not establish the Enclave's leadership, its full territory, or whether these two had formal authority to speak for it. The woman and the fox-eared Toad are not given names that the archive can safely assign. ‘Konathin’ enters the exchange, as does an unclear phrase about ‘Toad ie Fox’; who said which name and whom it referred to remain unresolved.

The stakes were clearer than the introductions. The pair said Fawful's Beans were preparing to summon a dragon and that the ritual involved a sacrifice. They were there to stop it. The conversation then reached backward toward Bowser's Castle: the dragon might be the one used there before 1035. The recollection moves from uncertainty to confidence, but no identifying feature or record is produced. This is a lead, not a match.

Bones offered to help for money. The notes record a **20-gold payment** from the woman. That is an event transaction, not a reconciled purse total. The camp-side gold exchange later in the account has no reliable amount or recipient, so Waluigi does not add a second invented number to it.
sections.waluigi_note: The name ‘Emerald Enclave’ is enough to open a file. It is not enough to invent a leader, a map, or an admission policy beyond the one the witnesses described.

sections.name: VI. The Borrowed Bean Disguise and the Broken Window
sections.imageCaption: Bones leaves the shorts behind while wearing the rest of an unnamed guard's outer clothing; the broken window is the recorded exit.
sections.overview:
Bones took the clothes from an unnamed man and copied the man's outward look. The exception is singled out in the notes: **everything but the shorts.** The shorts stayed behind. Bones wore the rest as a Bean guard disguise; no name, rank, or unit was attached to the person whose clothes he borrowed.

He saw two hooded figures and a Magikoopa shape. The account does not identify either hooded person or say whether the Magikoopa was a guard, a prisoner, or a witness. Bones took the broken window as an exit and jumped through it.

The woman and the fox-eared Toad were later taken by guards. A fight broke out among the people in that arrest, but the notes do not assign a victor or say whether anyone was freed. Bones did not stay to settle it. He had a disguise, a gap, and more of the compound between him and the doors than he had a moment earlier.
sections.waluigi_note: A disguise is only as good as the clothes you keep. The shorts were not part of the plan. Waluigi will not ask for further clarification.

sections.name: VII. Fawful's Sacrifice and the Mustard-Drone Pursuit
sections.imageCaption: Fawful directs the pursuit while Bones turns from a hulking Bean and a separate clockwork drone vents mustard into the passage.
sections.overview:
Fawful announced that the preparations were ready and that he had a sacrifice. A hulking Bean grabbed Bones. Bones drove his shortsword into the Bean's chest, hoping the poison would take effect. The notes give no saving throw, reaction, or confirmed result; the attack is recorded, and the poison's outcome is not.

**Fawful wound up a separate clockwork drone.** It spat mustard across the passage and across Bones. Fawful's pursuit widened: Bean forces closed in, the drone kept spraying, and Bones was grabbed again from behind. He slashed for room, bore through the hold, and bolted. The machine is not the hypno-helmet drone; the record treats them as separate devices because it describes separate attacks and does not say they are one chassis.

Fawful then brought the older woman and the fox-eared Toad out as backup. The two were held against a wall and hit with the mustard spray while the pursuit continued. Bones saw the scene, judged that the pair could manage themselves, and left while the guards were occupied. That judgment is his, not proof that either one escaped.

He ran into the trees, climbed, and got out of the immediate chase. No ritual completion is observed. No sacrifice is confirmed. Fawful's declared preparation and the dragon that appears later remain adjacent facts, not a proven cause-and-effect chain.
sections.waluigi_note: Poison hoped for is not poison proven. A dragon appearing later is not proof that the ritual summoned it. The file keeps both distinctions, even if Fawful does not.

sections.name: VIII. Goblin Fire, Waterball, and an Archie Bot's Recruitment
sections.overview:
Bones reached an unnamed goblin camp. He stayed apart from the goblins and waited as the light went; the notes do not name the camp or establish a route back to Arunedeal. A fart-spray gag appears in this camp-side sequence, but the source does not make its user, target, or effect clear. The filing keeps the beat without assigning it to Bones, the goblins, or the Archie-like figure, and does not treat it as a separate weapon or held item. When the goblins lit a fire, a figure they called an **Archie bot** stood near it.

The bot used a water trick to put out the fire. The shout is filed as heard: **‘WATERBALL!’** The goblins asked for Archie Miser's blessing, and the bot answered with the kind of pitch that turns a camp into a job interview: it said that having a bandit on their team mattered, that they needed it to win, and that they should keep paying it. The goblins accepted the pitch and showered the figure with bones and gold. The account does not count the coins or say whether any of that payment went to Bones.

The machine is filed as an ‘Archie bot’ because that is what the camp called it. Nothing in this scene proves that it is Archie Miser, that Archie Miser was inside it, or that the dragon's passenger is the same person. The separate Shadowfell/TOADALNAEC account dated 1 Aethel stays where it is.
sections.waluigi_note: The fart-spray gag is on the record; its target is not. Waluigi will not guess which camp member had the can, or what the can did.

sections.name: IX. The Dragon Comes for Archie
sections.imageCaption: A dragon arrives at the goblin fire; the portrait reference is a possible visual comparison to the Bowser's Castle record, not an identity finding.
sections.overview:
The trees shook. A roar followed, and a dragon crossed overhead before landing beside the camp. It asked, **‘WHERE IS ARCHIE? I WAS SUMMONED.’** The dragon also claimed, **‘I BETRAYED THE BEANS FOR THE TOAD GOD.’** The account does not name the summoner or establish that the dragon was the one Fawful had promised.

The camp's Archie-like figure went with it. The dragon offered training and an ‘Omega Fireball’; the exchange mentions that Archie had failed a mission in Feyward. The figure began to object that it used water, then let the objection go. The dragon invited Bones to come too. Bones said he had no quarrel and declined. The dragon ended the exchange with **‘Green D to you,’** then left with the Archie-like passenger.

The departure is clear. The identities are not. The report's possible Bowser's Castle connection is added to the castle succession file as a question to verify, not as a finding that this is The Supplied Dragon. The passenger is not folded into Archie Miser's existing status, and the dragon's allegiance to the Toad God is recorded as its claim, not a permanent contract.
sections.waluigi_note: The dragon left with an Archie. The archive still does not know which Archie, who summoned the dragon, or whether ‘betrayed the Beans’ is a confession, a boast, or a new contract.

sections.name: X. An Hour with the Map, Then Another Tree
sections.overview:
Bones did not take the dragon's invitation. He slept in the trees, still wearing the borrowed Bean disguise. At the final beat, he had a map and spent one hour measuring it. The notes do not name the route, the map's origin, its scale, or its destination. The archive records the object without drawing a road it never saw: [[prop:prop_bones_one_hour_map|the one-hour map docket]].

This is where the session stops. Bones is alive, outside the compound, disguised, and not on the Legion wall's doorstep anymore. The woman and her companion have no confirmed outcome; the victim of the hypno-helmet has no confirmed outcome; Fawful's ritual has no confirmed outcome; the dragon's identity and the passenger's identity remain open. The map is measured. The next direction is not.
sections.waluigi_note: One hour was measured. The route was not transcribed. Waluigi will not draw a shortcut because the blank page looks lonely.

aftermath: Bones exits the session in a Bean guard disguise and sleeps in trees with a map he measured for one hour. The current position of the woman and fox-eared companion, the hypno-drone victim, the ritual site, and the two drones is unknown. The dragon leaves with a figure called Archie, but the file does not equate that figure with Archie Miser or the dragon with The Supplied Dragon. The 20-gold cottage payment is recorded; the camp-side gold exchange is unquantified and unattributed, so the wallet is not reconciled.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. A ritual is not consent.** Two armed guards, locked doors and an explanation called ‘bonding’ do not turn a holding room into a voluntary event. The archive records their phrase and the physical locks; it does not accept the phrase as an answer.

**2. The machines are not one machine.** The 1035 Castle drone is a surveillance device. The hypno-helmet drone and the mustard-spraying clockwork drone are described here doing different things. They get separate entries, and neither is silently attached to the older drone.

**3. The Enclave is a name with a witness, not a full dossier.** The older woman invokes the Emerald Enclave and a closed admission policy. The record does not supply leadership, headquarters or an official roster. The possible fox-eared match to Toad ie Foxx remains a possibility; roster #73 stays unseen until the identity is actually established.

**4. The dragon's claim has two missing links.** The account ties a dragon to a later goblin-camp departure and recalls one at Bowser's Castle before 1035. It does not establish that they are the same dragon, nor that Fawful's ritual summoned this one. The Supplied Dragon file remains historical, and the Bowser Castle board gets a lead rather than a retcon.

**5. ‘Archie’ is not yet a person match.** The camp calls a figure an Archie bot; the dragon takes an Archie-like passenger. The existing Archie Miser record is a Shadowfell/TOADALNAEC account dated 1 Aethel. Waluigi will not teleport that person into the Material Plane by adjective.

**6. Bones's money is not 20 gold.** The woman pays 20 gold. Bones already had 17 gold on the last recorded wallet, but the camp-side gold exchange is not quantified or assigned cleanly. The wallet records the old reconciled amount and a warning; it does not pretend that the final balance is known.

**7. The last frame is the one to carry forward.** Bones has the borrowed outer clothes, not the shorts; he is in the trees, and he has spent an hour measuring a map whose route the archive cannot see. That is enough for continuity. It is not enough to name the next place.
